pages.title: About the Author
pages.excerpt: A fixture author chapter for the reader theme.
pages.content:
I work on software teams that turn new technical systems into usable, durable products. The through-line is helping people understand what the machine is doing, what it needs from them, and where the work should go next.

This fixture page is intentionally not a mirror of the live site. It gives the theme stable prose, inline reader highlights, and normal Gutenberg blocks to render while the future content model evolves.

Good tools should make the next right action easier to see.

posts.title: Notes on Reader-Shaped Websites
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay about reader interfaces.
posts.content:
A reader-shaped website can borrow from books without pretending the browser is paper. The useful parts are progress, focus, return paths, and a content model that respects chapters.

The less useful part is fake pagination. Real web reading still has to handle font changes, viewport changes, zoom, assistive technology, and links that move the reader somewhere else.

posts.title: Structured Projects Beat Page Cards
posts.excerpt: A fixture essay about moving project content into a CPT.
posts.content: Project cards are easy to draw once and hard to reuse later. A project post type gives each entry a title, URL, summary, status, grouping, and body that can be queried wherever the theme needs it.
